name: Venus
lede: A greenhouse runaway under a thick CO₂ sky — radar peels back the clouds to reveal a volcanic highland world.

landmark.label: Maxwell Montes
landmark.blurb: The highest mountain range on Venus, rising about 11 km above the mean planetary radius in Ishtar Terra.

missions.name: Venera landers
missions.note: Soviet surface images and pressure/temperature data before landers failed in the heat.

missions.name: Magellan
missions.note: Global synthetic-aperture radar map of nearly the entire surface.

missions.name: Parker Solar Probe
missions.note: Visible-light images of Venus's nightside glow during gravity assists.

researchNotes: Venus is similar in size to Earth but rotates retrograde and very slowly. Surface pressure is about 92 bar, and mean surface temperature exceeds 460 °C.
Magellan radar revealed continents, rift valleys, and volcanic plains. Maxwell Montes is the tallest highland; many features are named for women in mythology and history.
The dense atmosphere and sulfuric acid clouds hide the surface in visible light — radar and infrared are the primary remote-sensing tools.
folklore: Named for the Roman goddess of love. Evening and morning star lore is observational astronomy, not a second planet.
carlFocus: Stress Magellan radar, Maxwell Montes, runaway greenhouse, and retrograde spin. Distinguish myth names from spacecraft facts.
